decision.summary: The Fed cut its policy rate by 25 basis points, to 1%. The vote was 11-1. Dissenting: Robert T. Parry.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 1 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The Federal Open Market Committee decided to keep its target for the federal funds rate unchanged at 1-1/4 percent.”

changes.quote: In a related action, the Board of Governors approved a 25 basis point reduction in the discount rate to 2 percent.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: The Committee continues to believe that an accommodative stance of monetary policy, coupled with still robust underlying growth in productivity, is providing important ongoing support to economic activity.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Recent signs point to a firming in spending, markedly improved financial conditions, and labor and product markets that are stabilizing.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: The economy, nonetheless, has yet to exhibit sustainable growth.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: With inflationary expectations subdued, the Committee judged that a slightly more expansive monetary policy would add further support for an economy which it expects to improve over time.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

tone_quotes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 1 percent.

The Committee continues to believe that an accommodative stance of monetary policy, coupled with still robust underlying growth in productivity, is providing important ongoing support to economic activity.
The Committee perceives that the upside and downside risks to the attainment of sustainable growth for the next few quarters are roughly equal.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 12.26% APR, a 25 bp cut lowers monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3.38% and moved +9 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 5.21% would rise by about $16.73 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year less in interest.
Unemployment was 6.1%, and employers added an average of -81k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.9% over the past year (May 2003); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.6%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.1% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +16 bp on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is dovish (leaning toward lower rates).
